cards.subject: Physics
cards.question: State Lenz's law.

items.label: Says the induced current / emf OPPOSES
items.tip: Use the word 'opposes' and say it is the INDUCED current or emf.

items.label: Names the cause: the CHANGE in magnetic flux
items.tip: Say what is opposed: the change in magnetic flux that produces it.

cards.model: The direction of the induced current (or emf) is such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that produces it.
mistakes: Writing 'opposes the magnetic field' instead of 'opposes the change in flux'.

traps.msg: Lenz's law opposes the CHANGE in flux, not the magnetic field itself.

cards.source: Question type from uploaded TN papers. Key drafted by Claude. Teacher check pending.

peerSamples.label: Sample A
peerSamples.text: Lenz law says the induced current always opposes the change in magnetic flux that produces it.

peerSamples.label: Sample B
peerSamples.text: The induced emf is opposite to the magnetic field.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.question: Define optical path length.

items.label: Defines it using refractive index and geometric path (product)
items.tip: Say 'product of refractive index and the actual (geometric) path'.

items.label: Gives the formula: optical path = n × d (or μd)
items.tip: Write the formula with symbols explained: Δ = nd.

cards.model: Optical path length is the product of the refractive index of the medium and the geometric path length travelled by light in it: Δ = nd. It equals the distance light would travel in vacuum in the same time.
mistakes: Writing only 'the path of light' without refractive index.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.topic: Gauss's law: infinitely long charged wire
cards.question: Using Gauss's law, derive the electric field due to an infinitely long straight uniformly charged wire.

items.label: Cylindrical Gaussian surface (coaxial, radius r, length l)
items.tip: Say 'cylindrical Gaussian surface' and draw it with r and l.

items.label: States Gauss's law (flux = q enclosed / ε0)
Flux only through the curved surface (ends: E ⟂ dA, flux = 0)
items.tip: Say why the two flat ends give zero flux.

items.label: Final result E = λ / (2π ε0 r)

cards.model: Take a cylindrical Gaussian surface of radius r and length l coaxial with the wire. By symmetry E is radial. Flux through the two flat ends is zero (E ⟂ dA). Through the curved surface flux = E(2πrl). By Gauss's law E(2πrl) = λl/ε0, so E = λ/(2πε0 r).
mistakes: Forgetting to draw the Gaussian surface.
Not explaining why end flux is zero.
Dropping ε0 in the final answer.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.question: Describe the Mond carbonyl process used for refining crude nickel.

items.label: Ni reacts with CO at about 330–350 K to form Ni(CO)4
items.tip: Write the equation Ni + 4CO → Ni(CO)4 and the temperature.

items.label: Ni(CO)4 is volatile, so it separates from the impurities
items.tip: Say it is volatile and leaves the impurities behind.

items.label: Heated at 450–470 K it decomposes to pure Ni and CO

cards.model: Impure Ni + 4CO (330–350 K) → Ni(CO)4 (volatile). Ni(CO)4 is heated at 450–470 K and decomposes: Ni(CO)4 → Ni (pure) + 4CO. The CO is recycled.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.question: Differentiate between tetrahedral voids and octahedral voids.

points.label: Number per atom: 2 tetrahedral voids, 1 octahedral void per atom
Coordination: surrounded by 4 spheres vs 6 spheres
Size: tetrahedral is smaller (radius ratio 0.225–0.414); octahedral is larger (0.414–0.732)
Formation: sphere sits in the dip of 3 spheres vs two opposite triangular voids

cards.model: Tetrahedral void: 2 per atom, surrounded by 4 spheres (CN 4), smaller (radius ratio 0.225–0.414). Octahedral void: 1 per atom, surrounded by 6 spheres (CN 6), larger (radius ratio 0.414–0.732).
mistakes: Writing only one side of each difference.

cards.subject: Biology
cards.question: Explain the principle of insertional inactivation used to select recombinant bacteria.

items.label: Foreign DNA inserted inside the lacZ (β-galactosidase) gene inactivates it
items.tip: Name the gene (lacZ) and say the insert disrupts it.

cards.subject: Biology
cards.question: Write a short note on heterosis (hybrid vigour).

items.label: Definition: the hybrid (F1) is superior to its parents
items.tip: Say 'F1 hybrid superior to both parents'.

items.label: Cause: dominance / over-dominance hypothesis
items.tip: Name at least one hypothesis (dominance or over-dominance).

items.label: Example or importance (yield, hybrid maize, lost in F2)
items.tip: Give one example such as hybrid maize, or the use (higher yield).

cards.model: Heterosis is the superiority of the F1 hybrid over both its parents in vigour, size and yield. It is explained by the dominance and over-dominance hypotheses. Example: hybrid maize. The vigour is lost in the F2 generation.

cards.subject: Biology
cards.question: Differentiate between active immunity and passive immunity.

items.label: Any five differences (1 mark each)

points.label: Antibody source: own body vs readymade from outside
How acquired: infection / vaccine vs antiserum, colostrum, placenta
Onset: slow vs immediate
Duration: long lasting vs short lived
Memory cells formed vs not formed
Booster / second exposure gives a stronger response vs not
Immune system activated vs not activated

items.tip: Write two-sided points: Active … / Passive … for each point.

cards.model: Active: body makes its own antibodies, slow onset, long lasting, memory cells formed, acquired by infection or vaccine. Passive: readymade antibodies given (antiserum, colostrum), immediate, short lived, no memory cells.
cards.source: Question type from uploaded TN papers. Key drafted by Claude. Teacher check pending.

peerSamples.label: Sample A
peerSamples.text: Active immunity: the body produces its own antibodies, it is slow and long lasting, and memory cells are formed. Passive immunity: readymade antibodies are given from outside, it is immediate but short lived and no memory cells are formed. Active immunity is gained by vaccination or infection, passive by colostrum or antiserum.

peerSamples.label: Sample B
peerSamples.text: Active immunity is good for the body and passive immunity is also good for the body.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.question: A 5 m ladder leans on a wall. Its foot slides away at 2 m/s. How fast is the top sliding down when the foot is 4 m from the wall?

items.label: Relation x² + y² = 25 and y = 3 when x = 4
items.tip: Write the relation and find y = 3.

items.label: Answer 8/3 m/s (decreasing), with unit
items.tip: Number AND unit; say the height is decreasing.

cards.model: x² + y² = 25; at x = 4, y = 3. 2x(dx/dt) + 2y(dy/dt) = 0 → 4(2) + 3(dy/dt) = 0 → dy/dt = −8/3 m/s. The top slides down at 8/3 m/s.

traps.msg: The height is DECREASING, so dy/dt is negative (−8/3 m/s).
